summary: Perry County, IL, 100-foot fire tower under construction in August 1936 two miles north of Pinckneyville; listed as gone; no later record found.

facts.design: Fire lookout tower about 100 feet tall (1936 report)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Reported under construction on August 22, 1936; the completion date is not given in the sources read

evidence.supports: 100-foot tower for the forestry service under construction two miles north of Pinckneyville in August 1936
evidence.quote: A 100-foot tower to be used as a fire lookout station for the forestry service was under construction two miles north of here today.

evidence.supports: view of 13 miles in any direction from the tower
evidence.quote: From the tower an observer can see 13 miles in any direction.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources were found, and no search turned up staffing, completion, agency or removal records. The 1936 report says two miles north of here; the Pinckneyville name comes from the page heading, since the quoted report carries no dateline. The report names only the forestry service, so no agency is given. The 30.5 m height matches the report's 100 ft. The newspaper name, the August 22, 1936 date and the FFLA name Oak Grove were confirmed on the source pages. The FFLA point (38.11608, -89.39031) was not checked against the report's location. The Pinckneyville Public Library and city fire department history pages were read and mention no lookout tower.
